name: Linear algebra
title: Linear algebra essentials
intro: Linear algebra studies vectors, matrices and linear maps — the language of systems of equations, computer graphics, data and much of advanced maths. These lessons build intuition for vectors and matrices, solving Ax = b, determinants, eigenvalues and what a linear transformation does to space. Comfort with high-school algebra is enough to begin.

lessons.title: Vectors
lessons.summary: Arrows and lists of numbers; addition and scalar multiplication.

sections.p: A vector in the plane or space can be drawn as an arrow and written as a column (or row) of components. In R², v = ⟨v₁, v₂⟩. Two vectors are equal when corresponding components match; position of the arrow can slide (free vector).
Add componentwise; scale by multiplying each component. Geometrically, addition is tip-to-tail; scaling stretches or flips.
The zero vector 0 has all components 0. Length (Euclidean norm) ‖v‖ = √(v₁² + v₂² + …). A unit vector has length 1.
u · v = u₁v₁ + u₂v₂ + … = ‖u‖ ‖v‖ cos θ. Zero dot product means orthogonal (perpendicular) when neither is zero.

lessons.title: Matrices
lessons.summary: Rectangular arrays; addition, scalar mult and matrix–vector products.

sections.p: An m × n matrix has m rows and n columns. Entry aij sits in row i, column j. Matrices store linear data: coefficients of systems, pixel grids, or the action of a linear map.
Same shape required for addition: add entrywise. Scale entrywise. These match vector operations on the “big vector” of all entries.
If A is m × n and x is in Rⁿ (column), Ax is in Rᵐ. Each entry of Ax is a dot product of a row of A with x. Columns of A are the images of the standard basis vectors.
AB is defined when A is m × n and B is n × p; result is m × p. Entry (i,j) is row i of A dot column j of B. In general AB ≠ BA.

lessons.title: Systems Ax = b
lessons.summary: Linear systems as matrix equations; row reduction idea.

sections.p: The system 2x + y = 5, x − y = 1 is Ax = b with A = [2 1; 1 −1], x = ⟨x,y⟩, b = ⟨5,1⟩. Solving the system means finding x (if any) mapped by A to b.

Swap rows, scale a row by a nonzero constant, or add a multiple of one row to another. These do not change the solution set and lead to row-echelon or reduced row-echelon form (Gaussian / Gauss–Jordan elimination).

sections.p: Unique solution (pivot in every variable column); infinitely many (free variables); none (inconsistent row like 0 = 1).
Ax = b is solvable iff b lies in the column space (span of columns of A). The span of vectors is all their linear combinations.

lessons.title: Determinants
lessons.summary: A number that detects invertibility and signed volume scaling.

sections.p: For a square matrix A, the determinant det(A) is a scalar. Among other roles: A is invertible iff det(A) ≠ 0; |det(A)| is the factor by which A scales areas (2D) or volumes (3D).

sections.code:
det[a b; c d] = ad − bc
det[2 1; 0 3] = 6 − 0 = 6
det[1 2; 2 4] = 4 − 4 = 0  (singular)

sections.p: If det(A) ≠ 0, there is A⁻¹ with A A⁻¹ = I. For 2×2: A⁻¹ = (1/det)[d −b; −c a]. If det = 0, columns are linearly dependent and Ax = b fails for some b.
det(AB) = det(A) det(B). So det(A⁻¹) = 1/det(A) when A is invertible.

lessons.title: Eigenvalues intuition
lessons.summary: Directions that matrices only stretch; Av = λv.

sections.p: A nonzero vector v is an eigenvector of A if Av = λv for some scalar λ (the eigenvalue). A stretches or flips along that line without rotating it off the line.
Av = λv ⇒ (A − λI)v = 0 needs a nontrivial solution ⇒ det(A − λI) = 0. Roots λ are the eigenvalues.
sections.code:
A = [2 0; 0 3]
Eigenvalues 2 and 3
Axes e₁, e₂ are eigenvectors

sections.p: Diagonalizable matrices act simply in an eigenbasis: stretch by λᵢ along each axis. Used in differential equations, PCA, vibration modes and PageRank-style ranking.
For 2×2, eigenvalues satisfy λ₁+λ₂ = trace(A) and λ₁λ₂ = det(A).

lessons.title: Linear maps
lessons.summary: Functions that preserve addition and scaling; matrices represent them.

sections.p: A map T: Rⁿ → Rᵐ is linear when T(u+v) = T(u)+T(v) and T(cv) = c T(v). Equivalently T(0)=0 and T preserves all linear combinations. Every such map is multiplication by some matrix A: T(x) = Ax.
Rotations about the origin, reflections through a line through the origin, projections onto a subspace, and scalings are linear. Translations x ↦ x + b (b ≠ 0) are not linear.
ker(T) = {x : T(x)=0} (null space of A). im(T) = column space of A. Rank–nullity: dim(ker) + dim(im) = n for T: Rⁿ → Rᵐ.
Doing S then T is matrix product (matrices for the maps, in the appropriate order). This is why AB ≠ BA can matter geometrically: rotate-then-reflect ≠ reflect-then-rotate in general.

lessons.title: Independence, basis and dimension
lessons.summary: When vectors are redundant; coordinate systems that fit a subspace.

sections.p: Vectors v₁,…,vₖ are linearly dependent if some nontrivial combination gives 0 (one is redundant). They are independent if c₁v₁+…+cₖvₖ = 0 forces all cᵢ = 0.
A basis of a subspace V is an independent spanning set. Every vector in V has unique coordinates relative to a basis. All bases of V have the same number of vectors: the dimension dim(V).
Standard basis of R³: e₁,e₂,e₃. The plane x+y+z=0 in R³ has dimension 2. Columns of an invertible n×n matrix form a basis of Rⁿ.
Columns of A are independent iff Ax = 0 has only the zero solution iff (for square A) det(A) ≠ 0.

lessons.title: Geometry of maps in the plane
lessons.summary: Stretch, shear, rotate, reflect — reading a 2×2 matrix.

sections.p: A 2×2 matrix is determined by where e₁ and e₂ go: those images become the columns. Watching the unit square helps you see area change (|det|) and orientation (sign of det).

sections.code:
Scale: [2 0; 0 3]  stretches x by 2, y by 3
Shear: [1 1; 0 1]  pushes horizontally by y
Reflect over x-axis: [1 0; 0 −1]
Rotate θ: [cosθ −sinθ; sinθ cosθ]

sections.p: If det = 0, the image collapses to a line or a point (lower dimension). Information is lost; you cannot invert the map.
Matrices with AᵀA = I represent rotations/reflections: they preserve lengths and angles. Columns are orthonormal.
